name: PCOS
prevalence: ~5 million U.S. women of reproductive age
overview: PCOS (polycystic ovary syndrome) is a hormone condition that can cause irregular periods, extra facial or body hair, acne, and trouble getting pregnant. It's one of the most common reasons for missed periods in younger women, and it raises the chance of type 2 diabetes later on. There's no cure, but birth control pills, other medicines, and steady habits like regular exercise manage symptoms well — and most women with PCOS can still have children.
symptoms: Extra hair on the face or body
Weight gain that's hard to lose

drugs.name: Combined birth control pills
drugs.note: First-line treatment that regulates periods and improves acne and excess hair.

drugs.name: Metformin (Glucophage)
drugs.note: Improves the body's insulin response and can help restore regular cycles.

drugs.name: Spironolactone (Aldactone)
drugs.note: Reduces acne and unwanted hair growth.

drugs.name: Letrozole (Femara)
drugs.note: First-choice pill to help with ovulation when trying to conceive.

redFlags: Sudden, severe pelvic pain — especially with nausea or vomiting — could signal a twisted ovary, so go to the ER right away.

resources.label: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists

name: Endometriosis
overview: Endometriosis happens when tissue similar to the lining of the uterus grows outside it — on the ovaries, fallopian tubes, or elsewhere in the pelvis. That tissue swells and bleeds with each cycle, causing painful periods, pain during sex, and sometimes trouble conceiving. It often takes years to get diagnosed, so speaking up about severe period pain matters. Pain relievers, hormone treatments, and surgery can all bring real relief.
symptoms: Very painful periods that interfere with daily life
Pain with bowel movements or urination during periods
Heavy periods or spotting between periods

drugs.name: Ibuprofen / Naproxen
drugs.note: Usual first step for easing period pain.

drugs.name: Combined birth control pills
drugs.note: Lighten periods and calm endometriosis pain.

drugs.name: Norethindrone
drugs.note: Hormone pill that thins the misplaced tissue to reduce pain.

drugs.name: Elagolix (Orilissa)
drugs.note: For moderate-to-severe pain when other options fall short.

drugs.name: Laparoscopic surgery
drugs.note: Removes endometriosis tissue and can improve fertility.

redFlags: Sudden, severe pelvic pain with fever, vomiting, or fainting needs emergency care — go to the ER.

resources.label: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists

name: Uterine Fibroids
prevalence: Up to ~70% of women by age 50
overview: Uterine fibroids are noncancerous growths of muscle in the wall of the uterus. They're extremely common, and many cause no symptoms at all. When they do, the usual problems are heavy or long periods, pelvic pressure, and frequent urination. Fibroids almost never turn into cancer, and they often shrink on their own after menopause. Treatments range from medicines that lighten bleeding to procedures that remove or shrink the fibroids themselves.

drugs.name: Ibuprofen / Naproxen
drugs.note: Eases cramping and mild pain.

drugs.name: Hormonal birth control
drugs.note: Lightens heavy periods, though it doesn't shrink fibroids.

drugs.name: Tranexamic acid (Lysteda)
drugs.note: Taken only during periods to cut heavy bleeding.

drugs.name: Leuprolide (Lupron)
drugs.note: Shrinks fibroids temporarily, often before surgery.

drugs.name: Myomectomy or fibroid embolization
drugs.note: Removes or shrinks fibroids while keeping the uterus.

redFlags: Soaking through a pad or tampon every hour, or bleeding with dizziness or fainting, is an emergency — go to the ER.

name: Menopause
prevalence: ~1.3 million U.S. women reach menopause each year
overview: Menopause is the natural point when periods stop for good — usually around age 51 in the U.S. The years leading up to it (perimenopause) can bring hot flashes, night sweats, sleep trouble, mood swings, and vaginal dryness as estrogen levels fall. It's a normal life stage, not an illness, but the symptoms are real and treatable. Hormone therapy and other medicines help many women feel like themselves again.

drugs.name: Estrogen / estrogen-progestin therapy
drugs.note: Most effective treatment for hot flashes and night sweats.

drugs.name: Vaginal estrogen
drugs.note: Treats dryness and discomfort with very little hormone absorbed.

drugs.name: Paroxetine (Brisdelle)
drugs.note: Non-hormonal option that reduces hot flashes.

drugs.name: Gabapentin
drugs.note: Can ease hot flashes, especially at night.

redFlags: Any vaginal bleeding after menopause isn't normal — seek same-day care to rule out serious causes.

name: Yeast Infection
prevalence: About 3 in 4 women have one at some point
overview: A vaginal yeast infection happens when a fungus that normally lives in small amounts in the vagina (usually Candida) overgrows, causing itching, burning, and a thick white discharge. Antibiotics, pregnancy, and diabetes can make one more likely. Yeast infections are very common, not a sign of poor hygiene, and not usually spread through sex. Over-the-counter creams or a single prescription pill clear most infections within a few days.
symptoms: Redness and swelling of the vulva

drugs.name: Miconazole (Monistat)
drugs.note: Over-the-counter cream or suppository used for one to seven days.

drugs.name: Fluconazole (Diflucan)
drugs.note: Single prescription pill that clears most infections.

drugs.name: Clotrimazole
drugs.note: Another over-the-counter cream option.

drugs.name: Terconazole
drugs.note: Prescription cream for stubborn infections.

redFlags: If you also have fever, chills, or pelvic pain, it may be a more serious infection — seek same-day care.

name: PMS & PMDD
prevalence: PMS affects ~3 in 4 menstruating women; PMDD about 5%
overview: PMS is the cluster of symptoms — bloating, breast tenderness, irritability, food cravings — that shows up in the week or two before a period and fades once it starts. PMDD is a more severe form in which mood symptoms like depression, anger, or anxiety seriously disrupt daily life. Both are common and very treatable. Tracking your symptoms across a couple of cycles helps your doctor confirm the pattern and find the right treatment.
symptoms: With PMDD: intense sadness, anger, or anxiety
Symptoms lift within days of the period starting

drugs.name: Ibuprofen / Naproxen
drugs.note: Eases cramps, headaches, and breast tenderness.

drugs.name: Sertraline (Zoloft) / Fluoxetine (Prozac)
drugs.note: First-choice medicines for PMDD mood symptoms.

drugs.name: Drospirenone birth control (Yaz)
drugs.note: Birth control pill that is FDA-approved for PMDD.

drugs.name: Spironolactone
drugs.note: Can reduce bloating and breast tenderness.

redFlags: If premenstrual mood symptoms ever include thoughts of self-harm or suicide, call or text 988 or go to the ER.

name: Cervical Cancer
overview: Cervical cancer starts in the cervix, the lower part of the uterus, and is almost always caused by long-lasting infection with HPV, a very common virus. It grows slowly, which is why it's one of the most preventable cancers: the HPV vaccine prevents most cases, and routine Pap and HPV tests can catch cell changes years before cancer ever develops. Found early, cervical cancer is highly treatable, often with surgery alone.
symptoms: Bleeding between periods or after sex
Pelvic pain or pain during sex

drugs.name: Surgery (cone biopsy or hysterectomy)
drugs.note: Main treatment for early-stage cancer.

drugs.name: Radiation therapy
drugs.note: Often combined with chemo for larger tumors.

drugs.name: Cisplatin
drugs.note: Most common chemo, usually given alongside radiation.

drugs.name: HPV vaccine (Gardasil 9)
drugs.note: Prevents the infections that cause most cervical cancers.

redFlags: Heavy vaginal bleeding with dizziness, fainting, or a racing heartbeat is an emergency — call 911 or go to the ER.

name: Ovarian Cysts
prevalence: About 8% of premenopausal women develop one needing treatment
overview: Ovarian cysts are fluid-filled sacs that form on or inside an ovary, usually as a normal part of the monthly cycle. Most cause no symptoms, are found by chance on an ultrasound, and go away on their own within a few months. Some cause a pelvic ache, bloating, or pain during sex. Cysts are almost always benign, especially before menopause, so doctors often simply monitor them and treat pain if needed.
symptoms: Dull pelvic ache or pressure on one side
Bloating or a feeling of fullness
Sudden sharp pain if a cyst ruptures or twists

drugs.name: Watchful waiting
drugs.note: Most cysts go away on their own within a few months.

drugs.name: Ibuprofen / Naproxen
drugs.note: Relieves pelvic ache while a cyst resolves.

drugs.name: Hormonal birth control
drugs.note: Helps prevent new cysts from forming.

drugs.name: Laparoscopic surgery
drugs.note: Removes large or persistent cysts through tiny incisions.

redFlags: Sudden, sharp pelvic pain with fever, vomiting, or faintness can mean a ruptured or twisted cyst — go to the ER.
